plan: This auction structure is equivalent to a second-price sealed-bid auction: the winner pays the second-highest bid, determined by the ascending clock exit points. In such mechanisms, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy—it neither costs you when you'd lose anyway (bidding higher just risks overpaying) nor forgoes profitable wins (bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities). Since my value is $31, I will bid exactly that amount to maximize expected profit.

This auction structure functions as a second-price auction: I exit at my sealed bid, and the winner pays the second-highest bid. In second-price auctions, bidding one's true value is the dominant strategy, as it maximizes expected profit regardless of others' bids. My value is $6, so bidding $6 ensures I win only when profitable (paying less than my value) and avoid overpaying. There's no incentive to shade or inflate my bid.

My value for the prize is $0. Since this is effectively a second-price auction (I pay the second-highest bid if I win), the optimal strategy is to bid my true value. Bidding higher risks winning and paying more than the item is worth to me, resulting in a loss. Bidding exactly $0 ensures I never overpay - if I win, I'd pay $0 (breakeven), and if I lose, I lose nothing. This is the dominant strategy given my value.
